name: Tate v. Doe / Palm Beach witness-litigation chain

findings.summary: Original state suit filed July 11, 2023 — directly correlated with escalation of the Romanian DIICOT indictment timeline. All five original defendants are persons who reported allegations to U.S. government channels (Embassy, military) or are the primary accuser and associates. The chain exhibits canonical SLAPP characteristics: targeting witnesses in parallel criminal proceedings, weaponizing discovery timing, publicizing unredacted filings to expose defendants to mob harassment.

findings.summary: Jane Doe = Emma Aida Gabbey (Delray Beach, FL), John Doe = Matthieu Martelly (Palm Beach County), June Doe = Aliona Untila (non-U.S. resident), Mary Doe = unnamed UK-resident Romanian/Moldovan woman, Liam Doe = U.S. Marine Corps sergeant (identity court-sealed). All five are persons with direct or reporting roles in the Romanian DIICOT trafficking investigation against the Tates.

findings.summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate filed 9:23-cv-81150 (S.D. Fla.) via notice of removal from Palm Beach Circuit, asserting diversity jurisdiction (28:1332) against five pseudonymous defendants: Jane Doe (Emma Gabbey), John Doe (Matthieu Martelly), June Doe (Aliona Untila), Mary Doe (UK resident), Liam Doe (Marine sergeant). Claims: defamation, defamation per se, false imprisonment, tortious interference, civil conspiracy, IIED. Damages >$5M.

findings.summary: Tate attorney Joseph McBride posted the original unredacted federal complaint on social media, exposing defendants' passport numbers, dates of birth, and family names to the Tate online audience. Defendants immediately received threats including extortion threats to release sexual content. Over 50 pages of threatening social media messages were filed as court exhibits.

findings.summary: Judge Robin Rosenberg (S.D. Fla.) dismissed Liam Doe (Marine sergeant) WITH PREJUDICE and remanded to Palm Beach Circuit. Dismissal basis: sergeant did 'what the law encourages' — reported suspected criminal activity to military superiors and U.S. Embassy in Bucharest (functional qualified privilege). Remand basis: Tates deemed 'stateless' under King v. Cessna — Romanian domicile since 2015 defeats §1332 complete diversity.

findings.summary: No Florida anti-SLAPP (§768.295) motion appears in public record for any case in the chain. Possible strategic reasons for non-filing: anti-SLAPP requires early adjudication before discovery, cutting off both sides' discovery access; defendants may have preferred to preserve discovery to build criminal-case corroboration. Open investigative question whether motions were filed under seal or withdrawn.
